title: KuCoin launches version 5.0 with AI and trading upgrades
body: KuCoin has unveiled KuCoin 5.0, a platform upgrade covering trading, asset management, and user experience. The update is part of the company's global brand initiative, “Trust, Built-in,” which builds on its existing “Trust First. Trade Next.” positioning. The upgrade spans six areas: compliance, technology, assets, user experience, artificial intelligence, and wealth management. According to KuCoin, the changes are intended to bring these functions together into a more integrated platform rather than focus on a single product or feature. The most visible updates include a redesigned interface intended to provide clearer navigation for different types of users, an AI service layer spanning the platform, and additional ways to trade and manage digital assets. KuCoin said it is also strengthening the technology, compliance, and asset infrastructure underpinning its services as it continues to develop the platform. “Trust should be something users can experience in every interaction—not only in how their assets are protected, but in how clearly, reliably and efficiently the platform works,” said BC Wong, CEO of KuCoin. “KuCoin 5.0 is an important step in translating our long-term commitment to trust into the product itself. By bringing our core capabilities into a more connected, intuitive, and intelligent platform, we are giving users greater confidence and control today while building the foundation for the next stage of digital finance.” What has changed in the user experience KuCoin 5.0 introduces several changes to the platform's interface and account management tools. Profile Center 2.0 features a redesigned layout with cards intended to make account information and frequently used functions easier to find. The upgraded sub-account system streamlines account creation and management while adding security controls. Enhanced K-line charts provide additional trading tools and real-time data, with settings synchronized across devices. The update also adds a color vision accessibility mode designed to make charts and other visual information easier to distinguish for users with different color vision needs. KuCoin cited an estimate of 360 million people worldwide experiencing some degree of difficulty distinguishing colors. The platform also offers Lite and Pro interfaces to accommodate users with different levels of experience and trading requirements. For eligible users with more advanced trading needs, KuCoin 5.0 introduces the Unified Trading Account (UTA), available to users at VIP1 and above. UTA brings spot, margin, and futures trading into a shared framework for fund allocation, margin, and risk management. According to KuCoin, this reduces the need to transfer funds between separate accounts and allows users to manage capital across eligible trading products within a unified account structure. AI services across the platform KuCoin 5.0 upgrades AI Assistant to version 5.x, introducing a unified interface for conversations, questions, and task completion across the platform. The assistant covers areas including market insights, Earn products, trading, customer support, and campaigns. According to KuCoin, the assistant uses page context and user activity to better interpret requests, recommend relevant services, and help users complete tasks. Connecting earning and trading KuCoin 5.0 also introduces changes intended to connect wealth management and trading more closely. These include additional wealth management products and benefits for VIP users, access to Earn products through sub-accounts, and support for selected wealth management assets within the Unified Trading Account (UTA). Main accounts and sub-accounts can participate in Earn while maintaining separate fund management. KuCoin also said KCUSD can be used as margin within UTA, reducing the need to move funds repeatedly between earning products and trading accounts. The user-facing updates accompany further development across KuCoin's compliance, technology and asset infrastructure. The company said the six areas covered by KuCoin 5.0 are intended to provide a more integrated platform while maintaining flexibility in how users access its services. KuCoin said the upgrade establishes a foundation for future platform development by bringing trading, asset management, and AI-based services into a more connected user experience. title: Trump Approval at 34% as Gas Prices Jump 41% Ahead of Midterms
body: The Financial Times survey , conducted by Focaldata among 2,275 registered voters from October 2-4, found that 59% disapprove of Trump's overall performance. His 34% approval rating remains near September's 33% reading, while more than two-thirds of respondents believe the U.S. economy is heading in the wrong direction. Economic management received considerably weaker marks than Trump's overall performance, with inflation emerging as a particular source of dissatisfaction. Separately, Focaldata's October polling showed Democrats holding an eight-percentage-point advantage among likely voters on the congressional generic ballot. Although national polling cannot determine individual congressional outcomes, the findings illustrate how affordability concerns remain prominent in voters' assessments ahead of November 3. U.S. Gas Prices Jump 41% as Diesel Exceeds $6 According to AAA , regular gasoline averaged approximately $4.36 per gallon on October 12, versus roughly $3.09 a year earlier. That represents an increase of around $1.27 per gallon. For a driver purchasing 60 gallons monthly, the difference amounts to approximately $76 in additional fuel expenses compared with October 2025. Diesel prices have also climbed sharply, reaching approximately $6.27 per gallon nationally. Higher diesel costs matter beyond transportation because trucks carry food, consumer goods and industrial materials across the country. Elevated crude prices and disruptions to Middle Eastern energy infrastructure have contributed to the increases, although refining capacity and regional fuel availability also influence pump prices. As Coinpaper previously examined, Trump's promises of cheaper gasoline face challenges when global oil prices remain elevated. Inflation and Midterms Put Economic Policy in Focus The affordability concerns come despite estimates suggesting relatively strong U.S. economic growth during the third quarter. However, GDP expansion does not necessarily translate into immediate improvements in household purchasing power, particularly when energy and housing remain expensive. The upcoming October 14 Consumer Price Index report will offer another measure of price pressures, with economists expecting annual inflation of approximately 3.7%. Persistent inflation could also complicate the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decisions, particularly if price pressures remain elevated alongside weakening employment conditions. With the November 3 midterms approaching, the latest polling and gasoline figures provide two distinct indicators of economic pressure: voters' perceptions of affordability and the rising prices households are paying. Whether those pressures ease will depend partly on developments in global energy markets and upcoming inflation data.

title: Norway fines Microsoft subsidiary Xandr $9.6 million over privacy violations with Grindr
body: Norway’s data protection regulator has hit Microsoft’s advertising arm Xandr with a 92 million kroner ($9.6 million) fine for sharing Grindr users’ sensitive data with advertisers without a legal basis. The penalty will be the largest the agency has ever imposed on a company. Datatilsynet, the Norwegian authority behind the ruling, claimed the data involved information that could reveal users’ sexual orientation. The final decision closes a case that has been ongoing in Norway for over six years. How Grindr data ended up with thousands of bidders The case involves real-time bidding, a process that sells ad space in milliseconds as a user opens an app. When an individual launched the Grindr app in Norway, their personal data was sent through Xandr and potentially shared with thousands of companies and firms in the advertising industry, according to Datatilsynet. These companies then competed to deliver targeted ads to the user. Because Grindr caters to gay, bisexual, trans and queer users, the regulator considered app usage alone enough to reveal a person’s sexual orientation. Under European data protection rules, that makes the information sensitive data that requires explicit consent to process. The Norwegian authority found that Xandr had failed to obtain the required consent. It also ruled that the company shared responsibility for handling the data with Grindr, instead of just acting as an intermediary. Xandr’s direct financial benefit from the data sharing was another key factor in assessing the magnitude of any fines. Blaming the app did not hold up Xandr argued that it assumed Grindr had already collected valid consent from its users, an argument that was rejected by the regulator. “Responsibility for data protection cannot be delegated to others,” Datatilsynet Director General Line Coll said in the authority’s statement, as quoted by Tech Xplore. The director claimed each company must independently ensure and be able to demonstrate that it has a legal basis for using the data it procures. Coll said the breaches were particularly serious, noting that the sensitive personal data of thousands of Norwegian users had been shared illegally. The data sharing took place between July 2018 and April 2020, before Microsoft acquired the business, then known as AppNexus, PPC Land reported. Xandr now has three weeks to challenge the ruling at an appeal. The Norwegian decision follows a similar case in France earlier in 2026, where the Conseil d’Etat upheld a €40 million fine against retargeting company Criteo, rejecting its claim that partner websites were responsible for collecting consent. The two decisions make clear that companies remain accountable for data protection, and cannot rely on partners to collect user consent. A complaint that started since 2020 in Norway The complaint was filed in 2020 by the Norwegian Consumer Council and privacy group noyb over Grindr’s data-sharing practices. It was one of three complaints lodged that year, targeting both the app’s handling of user data and the adtech companies that received it. Felix Mikolasch, a data protection lawyer at noyb, said the ruling could force greater accountability from adtech firms such as Xandr, whose operations are often largely unseen and unnoticed by the public, describing the decision as an important precedent for similar cases in a statement from the group. Finn Myrstad, director of digital policy at the Norwegian Consumer Council, said the decision puts companies that rely on user tracking on notice. The latest ruling comes after Grindr faced a similar penalty in Norway. In 2025, the country’s courts upheld a 65 million kroner fine against the app for illegally sharing users’ sensitive personal information. The fine targets a company that is valued at around $3.97 trillion, according to GuruFocus. However, noyb has also warned that the precedent could lose its intended effect if the European Commission’s proposed Digital Omnibus weakens how the GDPR treats online tracking IDs. This proposal is currently under consideration by the European Parliament and Council. The smartest crypto minds already read our newsletter. Want in? Join them .

title: Tether blocks $10M linked to CryptoBilis Ledger wallet theft
body: Tether has frozen $10 million of its USDT cryptocurrency after a theft drained up to $93 million in assets from Ledger hardware wallets sold by CryptoBilis, as the investigation into the money flow continues and Ledger claims the problem is isolated. Confirmed information provided by Ledger so far The French cryptocurrency wallet maker has yet to comment on the losses. Ledger has said that all cases the company has identified involve devices sold by CryptoBilis, a third-party vendor that operated in Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines. The company also stressed that there were no signs of compromise of Ledger’s systems, services and direct sales. A discovery added an element of physical tampering to the case of software-related vulnerabilities. On October 10, the firm stated that one of the affected users owned a device that had an unauthorized physical implant installed, which has become the first evidence of physical compromise of Ledger wallets in this case. The message for buyers from its side is very clear. If you have bought a CryptoBilis device within the last 90 days and did not configure it yet, leave it untouched. If you are using the device right now, transfer your coins to another device with a new recovery phrase. How investigators tallied the losses These figures are attributed to on-chain analysts rather than Ledger. Bitquery estimated that the attack involved $93.2 million siphoned off from 315 wallets on six separate blockchains, primarily USDT and TRON coins. The security platform YFarmX set a higher number, claiming the attack took away $94.5 million from 521 wallets on seven different blockchains. Both estimates were based on public chain data. According to Bitquery’s analysis, most of the stolen money is attributed to TRON at around $70.5 million, with another $16.8 million in Bitcoin and $3.7 million in Ethereum, and much smaller amounts in BNB Chain, Polygon and Solana. The operation is claimed to have been planned for months: the addresses involved in the theft were created on September 25 and made dozens of trial transfers until early October. The major transfer took place on October 9 when Bitquery claims the attackers rewrote the permissions for 30 wallets on TRON before transferring some 203.8 BTC from 111 Bitcoin wallets within a single block an hour later. This sort of operation can be carried out only if the attacker has the necessary keys. This is important since the issuers of the stablecoins are able to blacklist coins used for illegal activities. Bitquery, which verified the Tether freeze, reported that there was still about $81 million of traceable tokens on-chain as of October 11, but some funds have passed through the mixer services of Tornado Cash and Zcash. Pushback over an authorized reseller However, Ledger’s characterization of the situation as a CryptoBilis issue has not gone over smoothly. The reseller had an official badge of Ledger on their website, hence making Ledger responsible for this situation since, “It’s not a CryptoBilis incident, it’s a Ledger incident.” X user MyCryptoParadise told the company to “take ownership of this mess.” There is yet another side to the story from the history of the reseller. According to Arravind Prabu, one of the co-founders, CryptoBilis was acquired in March 2026, and the entire team transferred all system access during the acquisition, as quoted in Learning Crypto. The only new investor in the company was registered in China, as per the company’s reported records. So far, there have been no links made between the thefts and the ownership change and the investigation found no tampering with new investors. CryptoBilis has suspended sales and deliveries of all brands that it sells and shut down its brick-and-mortar stores in all three countries. The implant Mark Karpelès pulled apart Perhaps the most definitive description of the hardware can be given by the founder of Mt. Gox, Mark Karpelès. Karpelès disassembled a Ledger Nano X purchased in Malaysia and, as reported by Learning Crypto, discovered additional components that were hiding under the screen: a cellular modem, an eSIM and a tiny chip that would enable it to intercept what was displayed on the screen. When setting up the wallet, the recovery words are displayed on that screen. A component that can intercept the data from the display would allow the words to be sent using the mobile network and, as a result, the wallet to be recreated somewhere else and the money to be stolen. It still needs to be proven whether all of the devices contained those components. It should be noted that this case is distinct from another theft in March, which happened in April when the Ledger Live application in Apple’s App Store was used by phishers to steal at least $9.5 million. title: SkyAI sells half its SOL to fund $201M buyback and keep Forward out
body: SkyAI plans to spend roughly $201 million buying back up to 95% of its shares and warrants at $3.00 each. The company plans to sell half of the Solana treasury it spent the past year building to fund the buyback. The move essentially rejects a takeover bid from Forward Industries . Will SkyAI buy back its shares? SkyAI (Nasdaq: SKYA) has announced a $201 million tender offer to buy back about 95% of its shares. It’s offering $3.00 per share in cash, which is less than half of what early investors paid when the company’s crypto treasury was first set up. A year ago, SkyAI was known as Sharps Technology and functioned as a medical device distributor. An SEC-filed press release shows that it raised more than $400 million in a private placement on August 28, 2025, selling units at $6.50 each. Every unit included a share of common stock plus attached warrants, and the proceeds went into SOL, the native token of the Solana blockchain, in what the company referred to as the launch of one of the largest Solana treasuries. Investors were told the raise could reach $1 billion if all warrants were exercised. SkyAI says the $3.00 price represents a 65% premium over its October 9 close and more than a 100% premium to its 60-day volume-weighted average, however both numbers measure against a stock that has fallen far from where the treasury started. A September 2026 filing revealed that it held more than two million SOL with no debt; now, to fund the buyback, SkyAI is draining that treasury. The company said it has already sold about 1 million SOL, roughly half its holdings, and holds about 1 million SOL as of the announcement. It said it may keep selling depending on the market. SkyAI controlled the fifth-largest publicly traded Solana treasury at 2,009,494 SOL, worth about $207 million in September. SkyAI also said it had booked more than $12 million in staking revenue through June 30, with its validator yielding 6.01% against a 5.57% network average. What deal did SkyAI reject? The buyback doubles as a defense for SkyAI after its board rejected Forward Industries’ latest unsolicited proposal , concluding the bid undervalues the company . Forward, which calls itself the largest Solana treasury company and reported holding 8.5 million SOL at the end of September, has been pursuing SkyAI since June. Its first offer, on June 15, was 0.367 Forward shares for each SKYA share. That was about a 20% premium, or $1.55 per share, which SkyAI rejected. On September 15, Forward improved the offer to 0.306 shares, valuing SkyAI at about $2.13 per share, roughly a 50% premium at the time. SkyAI’s $3.00 cash offer is higher than that, and it’s paid in cash rather than Forward stock. At SkyAI’s September 18 annual meeting, Forward attempted to win over shareholders. However, all five of SkyAI’s directors kept their seats, even though each got more withheld votes than votes in favor because the rules only require a plurality. Shareholders also voted down SkyAI’s proposed equity incentive plan, 22.5 million to 5 million. SkyAI expects to commence its tender offer on or about October 15 and run it for 10 business days. It covers up to 46.37 million shares and up to 20.72 million pre-funded and strategic advisor warrants. The offer comes with the condition that at least 50% of each class of shares must be tendered. Another condition is that the price of SOL must stay above $100 throughout the offer period. SOL traded near $111 on October 11. SkyAI says the offer doesn’t depend on financing, since its cash and digital assets already exceed the maximum $201 million it could spend. It has hired MacKenzie Partners to handle shareholder information and collect tendered shares. The official offer documents are due to be filed with the SEC by October 15. title: Bitcoin Bull Market Signal Emerges Even as BTC Struggles to Break $84K
tags: AA News|Crypto News|Locals|social|SocialFB|Bitcoin (BTC) Price|Bitcoin Bull Run
body: Bitcoin has closed above its 50-week moving average for four weeks in a row. Analyst Ash Crypto sees that as a sign the bottom is in, yet the average still slopes down, and Bitcoin sits about a third below its all-time high. Bitcoin Holds Above a Falling 50-Week Average “Historically, this means the bottom is in and the new bull market has started,” Ash Crypto wrote in a post on X. The weekly chart attached to the post showed BTC near $84,000 against a 50-week average of roughly $77,000, after a low near $58,000 and a strong green weekly candle that carried price back above the line. That average is the mean of the last 50 weekly closes, which is about a year of trading. As CryptoPotato reported earlier, Bitcoin topped out near $87,000 on October 2, slid to around $80,000 last Thursday, and had been trading near $83,000 since a Friday rebound. But the latest CoinGecko data shows it passing $84,000, up about 1% in the last 24 hours and 9% on the month, but down 2% across seven days and 24% lower than where it was a year ago. A CryptoRus note on X reminded that an earlier short-lived push through $84,000 forced out nearly $83 million in short positions, bets on falling price that traders must close when it climbs. That forced buying can speed up a move but cannot sustain one alone, according to the note, which puts the market at “a decision point rather than a confirmed breakout.” Fund flows have not helped. Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $681 million in net outflows last week, the most since late June, including $487 million on Wednesday as the price dropped. Confirmation Still Depends on Demand Meanwhile, XWIN Japan sees conditions for a bottom improving but ties confirmation to sustained ETF inflows, stronger US spot buying and a continued recovery in demand. Its on-chain charts show exchange BTC reserves still low and whale holdings around 3 million BTC, while its Apparent Demand measure has climbed from deeply negative levels but remains below zero. The firm noted that markets have priced in roughly an 18% chance of an October Fed rate hike, with the November 3 midterms approaching. In XWIN’s words, “A correction can build the foundation for the next advance.” CryptoRus wants repeated four-hour closes above $84,000 on rising volume and says another rejection there would show positioning did more of the work than conviction. Furthermore, it said releases such as inflation data (CPI and PPI), retail sales, and jobless claims could change market liquidity quickly.
